newsitem.title: MEXICO: Kimberly Clark Mexico 6-mos net falls.
newsitem.headline: Kimberly Clark Mexico 6-mos net falls.

text.p: Kimberly-Clark de Mexico SA (Kimber) said it earned 924 million pesos in net profits during the first six months of the year compared with 1.148 billion during the same period of 1996.
It said in a statement its earnings per share during the year's first six months was 0.69 pesos, or $3.45 per ADR. A comparative figure was not available due to a five for one split on March 31.
The company, an affiliate of U.S. paper giant Kimberly-Clark Corp, said its six-month operating profits were 1.207 billion, down 13 percent versus the 1.380 billion during the year-ago period.

The company said its comparative results were slightly skewed because its six month results from last year included only one quarter of results from Crisoba, the Scott Paper SPL.TO subsidiary bought by Kimber at the end of the first quarter.
For comparative purposes, the company also issued proforma results that took into account the Crisoba unit during the whole period.
The company said sales volumes and market share both increased, but weak prices and a poor sales mix led to lower sales revenues in real terms.
